title: Longitudinal characterization of the sensory phenotype of lipohyperplasia dolorosa (LiDo) patients during weight loss and subsequent liposuction.
summary:
Lipohyperplasia Dolorosa (LiDo), also known as lipedema, is eponymously characterized by both a fat distribution disorder and pain. How pain changes with weight loss or liposuction of the abnormal fat tissue has not been well studied. 
Severely overweight LiDo patients usually need to lose weight in preparation for liposuction. A previous study showed a change in the perception of sensory stimuli in LiDo patients. The aim of this study is to investigate whether/how the thresholds of sensory impressions including pain perception change in the course of weight loss and subsequent surgical fat removal. 
The study will be performed non-invasively by means of quantitative sensory testing according to the DFNS protocol in combination with pain questionnaires in LiDo patients who are undergoing treatment for study-independent reasons and who are undergoing weight loss in preparation for surgery or surgical LiDo fat removal for study-independent reasons, as well as in corresponding overweight control subjects. Hereby, the influence of pure overweight and liposuction on pain should be determined.

interventions.name: Characterization of the sensory phenotype of obese lipohyperplasia dolorosa (LiDo) patients using quantitative sensory testing during weight loss.
Characterization of the sensory phenotype of normal-weight lipohyperplasia dolorosa (LiDo) patients using quantitative sensory testing before and after liposuction.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Generally: female, age between 18-40 years, present signed and irrevoked informed consent.
For LiDo patients for weight reduction: medical diagnosis Lipohyperplasia dolorosa (LiDo), coincident obesity BMI > 40, 
For the weight loss group: study-independent planned weight loss to achieve BMI <40 required for lymphatic liposculpture.
For LiDo patients for lymphologic liposculpture: physician diagnosis of lipohyperplasia dolorosa (LiDo), 
For the surgery group: lymphological liposculpture planned for study-independent reasons, no coincident obesity; BMI <40.
For obese patients: No medical diagnosis of lipohyperplasia dolorosa (LiDo), obesity BMI > 40.
Exclusion criteria:
Limitation of the ability to communicate (language barrier, cognitive barriers, ...).
Diseases affecting the sensory nervous system (e.g. Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, radiculopathy, injuries of nerves innervating the sensory area of different genesis, diabetic polyneuropathy, peripheral polyneuropathies of different genesis, etc.).
skin stresses on the areas of measurement
topical application of analgesics to the areas of measurement (e.g. plasters, creams, ...)
diagnosed coagulation or wound healing disorder
other known alteration in pain perception or another diagnosed pain disorder
Liposuction already performed prior to study inclusion
Pregnancy
